handbookNote: New Hampshire Driver Manual (DSMV 360, Rev. 07/19), State of New Hampshire Department of Safety, Division of Motor Vehicles. The current live dmv.nh.gov site (migrated to a new Drupal platform circa 2023-2024) blocks automated/datacenter access with an Akamai 403 and no longer hosts a state-authored driver manual at all -- its own 'Driver Education' page now links out to a third-party site (edrivermanuals.com) instead of an official DMV document, and the manual's old canonical URL (nh.gov/safety/divisions/dmv/forms/documents/nhdm.pdf) now 301-redirects only to the DMV homepage with no replacement document, confirmed by checking that redirect target across multiple 2024-2026 Wayback Machine snapshots. The manual text itself was therefore retrieved via the Internet Archive Wayback Machine directly from that official nh.gov/dmv URL (the last confirmed-good, full-quality capture, cross-checked against a second capture from March 2022 with matching content/length), which is the last full edition New Hampshire DMV published on its own domain. Full text (128,544 characters, all 12 sections plus the Test Your Knowledge review) extracted with pdftotext and saved to C:\claudews\passexamhq\temp\handbooks\nh\driver.txt (a new file, separate from the existing nh notary handbook files in that folder). Real exam mechanics CONFIRMED directly from the manual's own text (Section 1, Required Driver License Tests): 'Automated Knowledge Test: The knowledge test consists of 40 multiple choice questions pertaining to the rules of the road and general driving conditions. Testers have 40 minutes to complete the test... If more than 8 questions are answered incorrectly, the test will automatically end.' That is 40 questions, 40-minute time limit (timed), and a de facto passing threshold of at least 32/40 correct (80 percent), since the test auto-ends after more than 8 wrong answers. The current live DMV site's own pages (Driver Licensing, FAQs, Apply for your First License) were also checked and still describe the identical three-test structure (Vision Test, Knowledge Test, Road Test) with no numeric contradiction, but no longer publish the specific question count or passing threshold themselves -- so the 40-question/40-minute/32-correct figures should be understood as the last officially documented mechanics rather than a number re-confirmed word-for-word on today's live site. No independent confirmation of these exact numbers still being current in 2026 could be found elsewhere on the official domain, so this is flagged as the best-available confirmed-from-primary-source figure, not a guess. Content-depth rationale: this is a real but comparatively modest 42-page, 12-section manual (Driving in NH/licensing & driver-ed requirements, Driver License & Non-Driver ID info incl. Youth Operator 'Under 20' law, Dangerous Driving incl. fatigue/distraction/alcohol-drug law, Before Driving incl. seatbelts/child seats/helmets, Basic Driving incl. right-of-way/speed limits/stopping distance, Rules of the Road incl. signs/signals/markings, General Driving and Parking incl. turns/roundabouts/school buses/parking fines, Driving Safely incl. visual search/space management, Accidents and Financial Responsibility -- notably New Hampshire has NO mandatory auto insurance law, Driving Emergencies incl. skids/brake failure/tire blowout, and Sharing the Road incl. pedestrians/bicyclists/motorcycles/large trucks/Move Over law/work zones). Every specific number, statute citation, dollar fine, distance, percentage, and procedure in this manual was mined and turned into a grounded, individually-cited multiple-choice question; 213 distinct questions were written across 12 topic buckets, each grounded in and cited to specific manual text (quoted or closely paraphrased in source_note). This total is honestly lower than some other states' driver tracks because NH's manual, while broad, is less exhaustively itemized in a few areas (e.g. it describes a single Youth Operator license system rather than a multi-stage GDL permit/intermediate structure, and has no state-mandated insurance minimums to enumerate) -- no invented facts, no restated 'common driving knowledge' outside the manual, and no padding were used to inflate the count toward a round number.
